note: Illustrative sample worlds for the Student design preview (Main.dc.html). They are design fixtures, not application data or service contracts. Each scenario is internally coherent and dated; facts come from the v46 boards where cited, otherwise they are marked illustrative. The React app keeps its own shared world.

ste.desc: Vary flow rates and inlet temperatures across a two-pass exchanger, then derive the effectiveness–NTU relationship from your own readings.
outcomes: Determine log mean temperature difference from measured inlet and outlet conditions
Compare countercurrent and cocurrent arrangements at matched duty

assessment.name: Heat Exchanger — post-lab
assessment.desc: Four short questions on what you measured in the Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchanger simulation. One answer is written; your faculty marks it.
assessment.mix: 2 multiple choice · 1 true or false · 1 written answer

qs.text: What does the effectiveness (ε) of a heat exchanger compare?
opts: The actual heat transfer with the largest heat transfer possible
The hot-side flow rate with the cold-side flow rate
The overall heat transfer coefficient with the surface area
The hot fluid’s inlet temperature with its outlet temperature
qs.expl: ε = q ÷ q_max, where q_max = C_min (T_h,in − T_c,in).

qs.text: How is the number of transfer units (NTU) defined?
qs.expl: NTU = UA ÷ C_min — the exchanger’s size measured against the smaller heat-capacity rate.

qs.text: Fouling on the tube surfaces lowers the overall heat transfer coefficient U.
qs.expl: Fouling adds a thermal resistance in series, so U falls.

qs.text: Explain how fouling changes the exchanger’s performance, using what you observed in the simulation.
qs.expl: Fouling adds a resistance, so U and the heat duty fall at the same flow rates: the hot fluid leaves hotter and the cold fluid leaves cooler.

assessment.rahul4: In the WEB run I turned the fouling up and kept both flow rates the same. The hot fluid left hotter than before and the cold fluid left cooler, so less heat was passed across. Fouling is an extra layer of resistance, so U goes down and the effectiveness goes down with it. That is why exchangers are cleaned, or designed with extra area.
assessment.rahulFb: Good use of your own readings and the right cause. For full marks, link the fall in U to the NTU and effectiveness relationship you derived in the lab.
assessment.imran4: Fouling makes the tubes dirty so the exchanger works less well. It should be cleaned.
assessment.imranFb: You named the cause. Explain what changes — U, the heat duty and the outlet temperatures — and use your readings.
